proofs.proof_tex:
Fix an arm \(a\) and suppress arguments.  By the definitions of \(S_a,F_a,G_a,R_a\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
 S_a(h+u,q+m)-S_a(h,q)
 &=u+I_a(q+m)(Y-h-u)-I_aq(Y-h)\\
 &=I_am(Y-h)-u(I_aq-1)-I_amu\\
 &=F_a(h,m)-G_a(q,u)-R_a(m,u).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(h+u\in\mathcal H_a(P)\) because \(T_au=0\), and \(q+m\in\mathcal Q_a(P)\) because \(T_a^*m=0\).  Each generator is centered on its stated product domain: using the bridge equations and the definitions of the two adjoints,
\[
\begin{aligned}
 E F_a(h,m)&=E[I_am\{Y-h\}]=\langle m,g_a-T_ah\rangle_{\mathcal G_a}=0,\\
 E G_a(q,u)&=E[u\{I_aq-1\}]=\langle u,T_a^*q-1\rangle_{\mathcal H}=0,\\
 E R_a(m,u)&=E[I_amu]=\langle m,T_au\rangle_{\mathcal G_a}=0.
\end{aligned}
\]
Putting respectively \(u=0\) and \(m=0\) in the first display shows that pure treatment-bridge and pure outcome-bridge shifts generate \(F_a(h,m)\) and \(-G_a(q,u)\).  Direct cancellation also gives the four-corner identity
\[
 R_a(m,u)=S_a(h+u,q)+S_a(h,q+m)-S_a(h+u,q+m)-S_a(h,q).
\]
Multiplication by the nonzero sign \(t_a\), while holding the other arm fixed, therefore shows that every admissible \(F\), \(G\), and \(R\) generator belongs to the linear span of differences of elements of \(\Phi_P\).  Conversely, the first display decomposes every difference between two bridge-pair scores into such generators, arm by arm.  Taking linear spans and then \(L^2(P)\)-closures proves
\[
 \mathcal C_P=\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{\phi-\phi':\phi,\phi'\in\Phi_P\}.
\]
For a nonempty subset \(B\) of a topological vector space and any \(b_0\in B\), one has \(\operatorname{aff}(B)=b_0+\operatorname{span}(B-b_0)\).  Applying this elementary identity with \(B=\Phi_P\), using that \(\mathcal C_P\) is closed, yields \(\mathcal A_P=\phi_0+\mathcal C_P\).  All products invoked above are precisely those required to lie in \(L^2(P)\) in the statement, so every equality is an equality in \(L_0^2(P)\).

Write \(N=\ker A\) and \(N'=\ker A'\).  For a unit vector \(x\in N\), decompose \(x=P_{N'}x+y\) with \(y\perp N'\).  The reduced-minimum-modulus hypothesis for \(A'\) and \(A'P_{N'}x=0\) give
\[
 \mu\,\operatorname{dist}(x,N')=\mu\|y\|\leq\|A'y\|=\|A'x\|=\|(A'-A)x\|\leq\varepsilon.
\]
Taking the supremum over unit vectors in \(N\) proves the directed-gap bound \(\delta(N,N')\leq\varepsilon/\mu\).  Interchanging \(A,A'\) proves \(\delta(N',N)\leq\varepsilon/\mu\), and hence the asserted symmetric-gap bound.

For completeness, a closed-range operator and its adjoint have the same reduced minimum modulus.  Indeed, the restriction
\[
 A_0:N^\perp\longrightarrow\operatorname{ran}(A)
\]
is a bounded bijection, \(\|A_0^{-1}\|=1/\mu(A)\), and the corresponding restriction of \(A^*\) is \(A_0^*:\operatorname{ran}(A)\to N^\perp\); its inverse is \((A_0^{-1})^*\) and has the same norm.  Applying the preceding argument to \(A^*,A'^*\), whose operator-norm difference is again \(\varepsilon\), proves the two cokernel bounds.

If \(P_N,P_{N'}\) denote the orthogonal projections, then \((P_N-P_{N'})^2\) is block diagonal relative to \(N\oplus N^\perp\), with diagonal blocks \(P_NP_{N'^perp}P_N\) and \(P_{N^perp}P_{N'}P_{N^perp}\).  Consequently
\[
 \|P_N-P_{N'}\|^2
 =\max\{\|P_{N'^perp}P_N\|^2,\|P_{N^perp}P_{N'}\|^2\}
 =\max\{\delta(N,N')^2,\delta(N',N)^2\},
\]
which proves the projection assertion with the same bound.  Substitution of \(A=\widetilde T_a(P)\), \(A'=\widetilde T_a(P')\), operator-norm continuity, and the common positive lower bound \(\underline\mu_a\) gives both claimed projection convergences.

Finally, if \(P_N,P_{N'}\) have finite rank and \(\|P_N-P_{N'}\|<1\), then \(P_{N'}|_N\) is injective: \(P_{N'}x=0\) would imply \(\|x\|=\|(P_N-P_{N'})x\|<\|x\|\).  Thus \(\dim N\leq\dim N'\); reversing the roles gives equality.  The same argument applies to the cokernels.  None of these norm estimates supplies differentiability or a path realization, which proves the final limitation in the statement.

The finite-witness theorem proves on the stated relatively open chart that actual finite-support path scores have closed span \(\mathcal T_P=\mathcal C_P^\perp\).  Positivity and finite support make every finite-valued bridge score square-integrable, while bridge existence makes \(\Phi_P\) nonempty.

It remains to verify the derivative rather than define it.  Write, on either arm, \(B=B_a\), \(b=b_a\), \(d=P(W=\cdot)\), and choose any solutions \(Bh=b\), \(B^\top q=d\).  Along a differentiable finite-cell path in the chart, the identifying functional is \(\mu_a=d^\top h\).  Differentiating \(Bh=b\) and using \(B^\top q=d\) gives
\[
 \dot\mu_a=\dot d^{\top}h+d^\top\dot h
 =\dot d^{\top}h+q^\top B\dot h
 =\dot d^{\top}h+q^\top\dot b-q^\top\dot B h.
\]
If \(s\) is the cell score, the three terms on the right are respectively \(E[hs]\), \(E[I_aqYs]\), and \(E[I_aqhs]\).  Therefore
\[
 \dot\mu_a=E[S_a(h,q)s],\qquad
 \dot\theta=E[\phi_{h,q}s].
\]
This holds for every bridge pair, so every member of \(\Phi_P\) is a gradient.

If \(g\) is any other gradient, then \(E[(g-\phi_0)s]=0\) for every \(s\in\mathcal T_P\); hence
\[
 g-\phi_0\in\mathcal T_P^\perp=(\mathcal C_P^\perp)^\perp=\mathcal C_P.
\]
Conversely, adding any element of \(\mathcal C_P=\mathcal T_P^\perp\) to a gradient preserves its derivative representation.  Thus the complete gradient set is \(\phi_0+\mathcal C_P\), which equals \(\mathcal A_P\) by \(\mathrm{lem:normal-affine-identity}\).  Orthogonal decomposition gives
\[
 \phi_0=(\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0)+\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0,
 \qquad
 \phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0\perp\mathcal C_P.
\]
Hence the first term is the unique minimum-norm element of the closed affine set \(\phi_0+\mathcal C_P\), and squaring its norm proves both displayed variance formulas.

By \(\mathrm{lem:normal-affine-identity}\), the shifted-pair score is
\[
 \phi_{h+u,q+m}=\phi_0+
 \sum_{a=0}^1t_a\{F_a(h_a,m_a)-G_a(q_a,u_a)-R_a(m_a,u_a)\}.
\]
By the narrowed quotient-efficiency theorem, the unique minimum-norm gradient is \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0\).  Equality of the last two displays is equivalent, after moving terms across the equality, to the factorization equation in the statement.  This proves both directions of the attainment criterion.

For any shifted pair, its difference \(c=\phi_{h+u,q+m}-\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\) lies in \(\mathcal C_P\), whereas \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}\in\mathcal C_P^\perp\).  Pythagoras therefore gives
\[
 E[\phi_{h+u,q+m}^2]=E[\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}^2]+E[c^2].
\]
Failure of the factorization equation means \(c\neq0\), so the inequality is strict.  Finally, the pure and four-corner identities in \(\mathrm{lem:normal-affine-identity}\) generate a dense linear subspace of \(\mathcal C_P\); translating by \(\phi_0\) proves the asserted affine-ensemble approximation.

Marginalizing the latent variable in \(\mathrm{def:finite-witness}\) gives minimum observed-cell mass \(9/1000\), hence all \(36\) cells are positive.  In the coordinate orders \(z,w=0,1,2\), direct summation gives
\[
 B_0=\begin{pmatrix}109/800&57/800&3/100\\57/800&9/200&27/800\\3/100&27/800&39/800\end{pmatrix},\quad
 B_1=\begin{pmatrix}39/800&27/800&3/100\\27/800&9/200&57/800\\3/100&57/800&109/800\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
 b_0=(21/400,9/200,21/400)^\top,
 \quad b_1=(3/50,21/200,37/200)^\top,
 \quad d=(7/20,3/10,7/20)^\top.
\]
The upper-left \(2\)-by-\(2\) minor of each arm has determinant \(27/25600\).  Matrix multiplication gives
\[
 B_av=0,\qquad B_a^\top v=0,
 \qquad B_ah_a^{\mathrm{sel}}=b_a,
 \qquad B_a^\top q_a^{\mathrm{sel}}=d,
 \]
for \(v=(3,-7,3)^\top\).  Since the displayed minor is nonsingular and the determinant of each \(B_a\) is zero, both matrices have rank two and both null spaces equal \(\operatorname{span}\{v\}\).  Also
\[
 \theta(P^\star)=d^\top(h_1^{\mathrm{sel}}-h_0^{\mathrm{sel}})=1/5.
\]
On a sufficiently small neighborhood in the positive simplex, likelihood ratios relative to \(P^\star\) are bounded above and away from zero.  The transported operators are finite matrices with entries continuous in the cell probabilities.  On the rank-two locus their nullity and cokernel dimensions stay one, while continuity of singular values keeps the reduced minimum moduli bounded below by a positive constant.  Thus this neighborhood satisfies the transported chart conditions without injectivity or surjectivity.

On the neighborhood where those minors stay nonsingular, rank two is equivalent to the Schur-complement equation in \(\Xi\).  Conditional on rank two, \(B_ah=b_a\) is equivalent to the displayed outcome Schur equation, and \(B_a^\top q=d\) is equivalent to the displayed treatment Schur equation.  Thus \(\Xi=0\) is an exact local description of the joint model, not merely a linearization.

Let \(D=(F_0,G_0,R_0,F_1,G_1,R_1)^\top\) evaluated at the displayed bridges and null vector, let \(\Gamma=E[DD^\top]\), and let \(c=E[D\phi_{\mathrm{sel}}]\).  Differentiating the three Schur equations gives, up to nonzero row rescalings, respectively the linear forms
\[
 \dot P\longmapsto E[R_as],\qquad
 \dot P\longmapsto E[F_as],\qquad
 \dot P\longmapsto-E[G_as].
\]
The shared vector \(d\) is differentiated only once as the marginal of the joint cell law.  Exact cell summation gives
\[
\Gamma=\begin{pmatrix}
1323/500&-6/5&63/20&0&0&0\\
-6/5&343/5&-21&0&-21&0\\
63/20&-21&441/2&0&0&0\\
0&0&0&1323/500&6/5&-63/20\\
0&-21&0&6/5&343/5&-21\\
0&0&0&-63/20&-21&441/2
\end{pmatrix},
\quad
c=\begin{pmatrix}24/125\\8/25\\6/5\\-24/125\\8/25\\6/5\end{pmatrix},
\]
and
\[
 \det(\Gamma)=\frac{16253767998768573}{12500000}>0.
\]
Because the six normal functions are linearly independent, the six constraint differentials are independent on the probability simplex.  Choose six cell coordinates \(z\) on which their Jacobian block \(L\) is nonsingular and collect all remaining simplex coordinates as \(x\).  The following direct local construction realizes every derivative \((v_x,v_z)\) annihilated by the constraint derivative.  Put \(x(t)=x_0+tv_x\) and seek \(z(t)=z_0+tv_z+r(t)\).  Differentiability and the tangent equation give
\[
 \Xi\{x(t),z_0+tv_z\}=o(t).
\]
Set \(e(t)=\|\Xi\{x(t),z_0+tv_z\}\|=o(|t|)\).  For sufficiently small \(t\), continuity of the derivative makes
\[
 r\longmapsto r-L^{-1}\Xi\{x(t),z_0+tv_z+r\}
\]
a contraction, with Lipschitz constant at most \(1/2\), on the ball of radius \(2\|L^{-1}\|e(t)\).  It maps that ball into itself because its value at zero has norm at most \(\|L^{-1}\|e(t)\).  Starting at zero, its iterates are Cauchy by the geometric Lipschitz bound, and their limit \(r(t)\) is a fixed point.  Thus \(r(t)=o(t)\) and \(\Xi\{x(t),z(t)\}=0\).  This proves directly that every vector in the derivative kernel is the derivative of a model curve.  Strict positivity persists for sufficiently small parameter values.  A differentiable positive finite-cell curve satisfies
\(\sqrt{p_t}=\sqrt p\{1+t\dot p/(2p)\}+o(t)\) in \(L^2(\nu)\), so it is DQM with score \(s=\dot p/p\).  Therefore actual path scores span exactly the annihilator of the six normals, namely \(\mathcal T_{P^\star}=\mathcal C_{P^\star}^\perp\).  The same nonzero Jacobian minor remains nonzero on a relatively open positive neighborhood, proving the local rank assertion.

Solving the normal equations gives
\[
 \Gamma^{-1}c=left(
 \frac{16264}{229047},\frac{12512}{1145235},\frac{131512}{24049935},
 -\frac{16264}{229047},\frac{12512}{1145235},\frac{131512}{24049935}
 \right)^\top.
\]
The derivative calculation
\[
 \dot\mu_a=\dot d^\top h_a+q_a^\top(\dot b_a-\dot B_ah_a)=E[S_a(h_a,q_a)s]
\]
shows that \(\phi_{\mathrm{sel}}\) is a gradient on this finite chart.  Projection onto the tangent space and direct summation now yield
\[
 E[\phi_{\mathrm{sel}}^2]=\frac{4432}{1875},\qquad
 V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^\star)
 =E[\phi_{\mathrm{sel}}^2]-c^\top\Gamma^{-1}c
 =\frac{773723312}{334026875}.
\]

Every bridge pair is uniquely of the form \(h_a^{\mathrm{sel}}+c_av\), \(q_a^{\mathrm{sel}}+d_av\).  If its score change has coefficients \((x_a,y_a,z_a)\) on \((F_a,G_a,R_a)\), the algebraic identity gives
\[
 x_a=t_ad_a,\qquad y_a=-t_ac_a,
 \qquad z_a=-t_ac_ad_a=t_ax_ay_a.
\]
Attainment of the projected score would require \((x_a,y_a,z_a)=-(\beta_{F,a},\beta_{G,a},\beta_{R,a})\), where \(\beta=\Gamma^{-1}c\), but in both arms
\[
 \beta_{R,a}+t_a\beta_{F,a}\beta_{G,a}
 =\frac{410302072}{87437547015}>0.
\]
Thus no single pair attains the bound.  The sets \(\{(x,y,z):z=t_axy\}\) are closed, and the Gram norm is equivalent to Euclidean norm because \(\Gamma\) is positive definite; hence their distance from the projected coefficient is strictly positive.  Continuity of the cell moments, the nonzero Jacobian minor, the positive Gram eigenvalues, and the displayed nonzero obstruction preserves rank, tangent completeness, and strict nonattainment on a smaller relatively open positive chart.

The model inclusion follows immediately from
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}=\mathcal U_P\cap\mathcal L_{\mathrm{out}}\cap\mathcal L_{\mathrm{trt}}\) and
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CX}}=\mathcal U_P\cap\mathcal L_{\mathrm{out}}\).  Every path in the first model is consequently a path in the second, proving the tangent inclusion.

At the positive rank-two witness, the outcome-only model has, per arm, the rank-two Schur equation and the outcome-solvability Schur equation.  Their differentials are the \(R_a\) and \(F_a\) linear forms derived in the finite-witness proof.  The treatment-solvability equation, whose differential is \(-G_a\), is absent.  The principal Gram matrix for
\(D_{FR}=(F_0,R_0,F_1,R_1)^\top\) and its cross-moment with \(\phi_{\mathrm{sel}}\) are
\[
 \Gamma_{FR}=\begin{pmatrix}
1323/500&63/20&0&0\\
63/20&441/2&0&0\\
0&0&1323/500&-63/20\\
0&0&-63/20&441/2
\end{pmatrix},
\quad
c_{FR}=\begin{pmatrix}24/125\\6/5\\-24/125\\6/5\end{pmatrix}.
\]
This matrix is positive definite as a principal submatrix of the positive-definite six-normal Gram matrix.  Hence the same finite-dimensional path argument gives
\(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{CX},P^\star}=overline{\operatorname{span}}(F,R)^\perp\).  The derivative formula from the finite-witness proof remains valid at the base law because \(B_a^\top q_a=d\) there, even though treatment-bridge solvability is not imposed on nearby outcome-only laws.  Thus
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{CX}}=\phi_{\mathrm{sel}}-D_{FR}^\top\Gamma_{FR}^{-1}c_{FR},
 \qquad
 \Gamma_{FR}^{-1}c_{FR}=(8/119,8/1785,-8/119,8/1785)^\top.
\]
Direct substitution gives
\[
 E[\phi_{\mathrm{CX}}^2]
 =\frac{4432}{1875}-c_{FR}^\top\Gamma_{FR}^{-1}c_{FR}
 =\frac{30544}{13125}.
\]

For nested closed tangent spaces, write
\(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{CX},P}=\mathcal T_P\oplus(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{CX},P}\cap\mathcal T_P^\perp)\).  Projection of the larger-model canonical gradient onto \(\mathcal T_P\) represents the same derivative on every \(s\in\mathcal T_P\), and uniqueness in \(\mathcal T_P\) therefore gives \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\phi_{\mathrm{CX}}\).  Pythagoras proves the variance-gap identity.  Finally,
\[
 \frac{30544}{13125}-\frac{773723312}{334026875}
 =\frac{2166784}{200416125}>0.
\]
The difference between the two finite normal systems is precisely \(G\) modulo the common span of \(F,R\), proving the last characterization.

For finite equal-cardinality proxy supports, the conditional operator and its adjoint are represented, after the positive diagonal changes induced by the Hilbert-space weights, by \(B_a\) and \(B_a^\top\).  Nonsingularity therefore makes both operators bijective.  Hence their kernels are zero, the outcome and treatment bridge solutions are unique, and every \(F,G,R\) generator in \(\mathrm{def:normal-space}\) is zero.  It follows that \(\mathcal C_P=\{0\}\) and, by uniqueness, \(\Phi_P=\{\phi_{h,q}\}\).

Nonsingularity is open.  On a sufficiently small strictly positive neighborhood it persists, and both bridge equations are automatically solvable, so the local joint model imposes no equality constraint.  Every mean-zero finite-cell score is realized by \(p_t=p(1+ts)\) for sufficiently small \(|t|\); positivity and bounded likelihood ratios hold because the support is finite.  Thus \(\mathcal T_P=L_0^2(P)\).  The finite derivative calculation
\[
 \dot\mu_a=\dot d^\top h_a+q_a^\top(\dot b_a-\dot B_ah_a)=E[S_a(h_a,q_a)s]
\]
shows that \(\phi_{h,q}\) is a gradient.  Since the tangent space is all of \(L_0^2(P)\), that gradient is unique and is the canonical gradient.  Because \(\mathcal A_P\) is the singleton containing it, its minimum-norm element is the same function, completing the reduction.

theorem.statement: The answer to \(\mathrm{oeq:score-lifting-completeness}\) is negative under the frozen assumptions.  There is a dominated base law and a bounded likelihood-ratio chart satisfying every displayed operator, rank, closed-range, and bridge-existence condition for which \(\mathcal C_P=\{0\}\) but \(\mathcal T_P=\{0\}\subsetneq L_0^2(P)=\mathcal C_P^\perp\).  Hence chart richness, not merely operator continuity and locally constant rank, is necessary for reverse score lifting.
theorem.proof_tex:
Let \(Z,W,X\) be constant, let \(A\) and \(Y\) be independent \(\operatorname{Bernoulli}(1/2)\) variables, and let \(\nu\) be counting measure on the four \((A,Y)\)-cells.  Then \(p=1/4\) on every cell, so \(P\ll\nu\) and \(E[Y^2]=1/2<\infty\).  Take the allowed chart domain to be the singleton \(\mathcal V_P=\{P\}\), with, for example, likelihood-ratio constants \(c=1/2\) and \(C=2\).

Both \(\mathcal H\) and each \(\mathcal G_a\) are one-dimensional.  In scalar coordinates,
\[
 T_ah=h,\qquad T_a^*q=P(A=a)q=q/2.
\]
Thus both maps are bijective, have closed range and positive reduced minimum modulus, their transported versions are constant on \(\mathcal V_P\), and their nullities and cokernel dimensions are zero.  The bridges \(h_a=E[Y\mid A=a]=1/2\) and \(q_a=2\) exist.  Hence all frozen chart and bridge-existence conditions hold, and \(P\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\).

Since \(\mathcal N_a(P)=\mathcal K_a(P)=\{0\}\), every generator in \(\mathrm{def:normal-space}\) is zero, whence \(\mathcal C_P=\{0\}\) and \(\mathcal C_P^\perp=L_0^2(P)\).  On the other hand, any path with values in the singleton \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)=\{P\}\) is constant, so its DQM score is zero and therefore \(\mathcal T_P=\{0\}\).  The function \(s=2Y-1\) has \(E[s]=0\) and \(E[s^2]=1\); hence \(s\in\mathcal C_P^\perp\) but it cannot be approximated by finite linear combinations of actual path scores.  This is the required explicit witness and disproves the universal reverse inclusion.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
On the relatively open strictly positive rank-two finite-support chart around \(P^\star\) certified by \(\mathrm{thm:finite-witness-nonattainment}\), \(\Phi_P\neq\varnothing\), the observed joint-bridge functional \(\theta\) is pathwise differentiable, and every square-integrable bridge score is a gradient.  Every gradient belongs to \(\mathcal A_P\), and, for any \(\phi_0\in\Phi_P\),
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0
 =\operatorname*{argmin}_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2],
 \qquad
 V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\inf_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2].
\]
No such conclusion is asserted for an arbitrary bounded-ratio chart lacking a path-richness condition.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The universal claim cannot be supported after the explicit singleton-chart counterexample: the frozen chart conditions impose no path-richness. The replacement restricts the conclusion to the regular positive finite chart on which actual score lifting is proved rather than assumed.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
On the relatively open finite chart covered by the narrowed \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), fix \(\phi_0=\phi_{h,q}\in\Phi_P\).  A shifted pair \((h_a+u_a,q_a+m_a)_{a=0}^1\) attains \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\) if and only if there are \(u_a\in\mathcal N_a(P)\) and \(m_a\in\mathcal K_a(P)\) such that
\[
 \Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0=
 \sum_{a=0}^1t_a\{-F_a(h_a,m_a)+G_a(q_a,u_a)+R_a(m_a,u_a)\}.
\]
If the equation fails for a given shifted pair, that pair's score has variance strictly above \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\); finite four-corner affine ensembles are dense in the minimum-norm affine-hull solution.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The factorization argument is valid where the canonical-gradient projection has been established. The universal completeness premise fails, so the honest scope is the certified regular finite chart.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
In the transported coordinates, \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{joint}}(P)\subset\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CX}}(P)\), and therefore \(\mathcal T_P\subseteq\mathcal T_{\mathrm{CX},P}\).  At \(P^\star\), because \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{CX}}(P)\) retains the fixed-rank chart \(\mathcal U_P\), its normal space is \(\overline{\operatorname{span}}\{F_a(h,m),R_a(m,u):a=0,1\}\), not the span of \(F\) alone.  For the corresponding fixed-rank outcome-only canonical gradient,
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\Pi_{\mathcal T_P}\phi_{\mathrm{CX}},
 \qquad
 V_{\mathrm{CX}}(P)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)
 =\|\Pi_{\mathcal T_{\mathrm{CX},P}\cap\mathcal T_P^\perp}\phi_{\mathrm{CX}}\|_2^2.
\]
The additional joint-model normal directions are the nonredundant components of \(G\) modulo \(\overline{\operatorname{span}}(F,R)\).  Exact projection gives
\[
 V_{\mathrm{CX}}(P^\star)=\frac{30544}{13125},
 \qquad
 V_{\mathrm{CX}}(P^\star)-V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P^\star)
 =\frac{2166784}{200416125}>0.
\]
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current comparison is false in its own frozen model: the outcome-only comparator retains the fixed-rank chart, whose rank Schur equations contribute R normals. Projecting only on F produces the quoted number; projecting on the actual F-and-R normal space gives the corrected bound and gap. The replacement also removes source-hypothesis assertions not declared in the frozen proof spine.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: On a strictly positive finite-support chart on which each arm matrix \(B_a\) is square and nonsingular, \(T_a\) and \(T_a^*\) are bijective, \(\mathcal N_a(P)=\mathcal K_a(P)=\{0\}\), \(\mathcal C_P=\{0\}\), and \(\Phi_P=\{\phi_{h,q}\}\).  The chart is locally unrestricted, and its canonical gradient is \(\phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\phi_{h,q}\).  Thus the quotient construction reduces exactly to the ordinary unique-bridge score on this finite bijective endpoint.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: Bijectivity alone does not repair an arbitrarily path-poor chart, as the singleton-chart counterexample shows. The replacement states the reduction on a strictly positive finite chart where nonsingularity makes the model locally unrestricted and the tangent calculation is proved directly.

proposed.statement:
On the relatively open strictly positive rank-two finite-support chart around \(P^\star\) certified by \(\mathrm{thm:finite-witness-nonattainment}\), \(\Phi_P\neq\varnothing\), the observed joint-bridge functional \(\theta\) is pathwise differentiable, and every square-integrable bridge score is a gradient.  Every gradient belongs to \(\mathcal A_P\), and, for any \(\phi_0\in\Phi_P\),
\[
 \phi_{\mathrm{eff}}=\phi_0-\Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0
 =\operatorname*{argmin}_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2],
 \qquad
 V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)=\inf_{\varphi\in\mathcal A_P}E[\varphi^2].
\]
No such conclusion is asserted for an arbitrary bounded-ratio chart lacking a path-richness condition.
proposed.justification: On the explicit regular finite chart this identifies the complete gradient affine space and its minimum-norm element without a hidden score-saturation premise.
proposed.gap: The frozen operator conditions alone do not imply path richness; the theorem is therefore restricted to the chart where the tangent equality is derived from the finite constraints.
proposed.consumer: The finite chart supplies a valid variance-minimizing benchmark and an exact diagnostic for redundant-proxy implementations.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Update dependencies and free symbols to the narrowed regular finite-chart claim after the negative OEQ resolution.

proposed.statement:
On the relatively open finite chart covered by the narrowed \(\mathrm{thm:quotient-efficiency}\), fix \(\phi_0=\phi_{h,q}\in\Phi_P\).  A shifted pair \((h_a+u_a,q_a+m_a)_{a=0}^1\) attains \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\) if and only if there are \(u_a\in\mathcal N_a(P)\) and \(m_a\in\mathcal K_a(P)\) such that
\[
 \Pi_{\mathcal C_P}\phi_0=
 \sum_{a=0}^1t_a\{-F_a(h_a,m_a)+G_a(q_a,u_a)+R_a(m_a,u_a)\}.
\]
If the equation fails for a given shifted pair, that pair's score has variance strictly above \(V_{\mathrm{eff}}(P)\); finite four-corner affine ensembles are dense in the minimum-norm affine-hull solution.
proposed.justification: The equation is the exact finite-chart certificate for when one representative attains the affine bound.
proposed.gap: Outside a chart with proved tangent completeness, the expression remains only an affine-score optimization identity and is not an information-bound theorem.
proposed.consumer: The factorization residual is a computable certificate of bridge-pair inefficiency.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(a\in\{0,1\}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}positivity}\),
\[
 P(A=a)=E\{P(A=a\mid U,X)\}>0,
\]
so the following arm-specific conditional expectations are nonvacuous; equalities conditional on \(A=a,Z,X\) are understood \(I_a\,dP\)-almost everywhere.  Put
\[
 m_a(U,X)=E\{Y(a)\mid U,X\}.
\]
The conditional expectation in \(\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}bridge\text{-}compatibility}\) is well typed only for an integrable \(Y(a)\); thus \(m_a\in L^1(P)\).  On \(\{A=a\}\), consistency \(\mathrm{ass:causal\text{-}consistency}\) gives \(Y=Y(a)\).  Conditional exchangeability \(\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}exchangeability}\) gives
\[
 E\{Y(a)\mid U,X,A,Z\}=E\{Y(a)\mid U,X\}=m_a(U,X).
\]
Successive conditioning therefore yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 g_a(Z,X)
 &=E(Y\mid A=a,Z,X)\\
 &=E\{Y(a)\mid A=a,Z,X\}\\
 &=E\!\left[E\{Y(a)\mid U,X,A,Z\}\mid A=a,Z,X\right]\\
 &=E\{m_a(U,X)\mid A=a,Z,X\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here the first equality is the definition of \(g_a\), the second uses consistency, the third is the tower property, and the fourth uses latent exchangeability.

By the declared type of \(h_a^\dagger\), \(h_a^\dagger\in\mathcal H=L^2(P_{W,X})\), hence it is integrable.  The compatibility condition \(\mathrm{ass:latent\text{-}bridge\text{-}compatibility}\) says
\[
 E\{h_a^\dagger(W,X)\mid U,X\}=m_a(U,X).
\]
Moreover, \(\mathrm{ass:w\text{-}treatment\text{-}negative\text{-}control}\) implies, for this integrable function of \((W,X)\),
\[
 E\{h_a^\dagger(W,X)\mid U,X,A,Z\}
 =E\{h_a^\dagger(W,X)\mid U,X\}=m_a(U,X).
\]
Applying the tower property once more and comparing with the preceding display for \(g_a\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E\{h_a^\dagger(W,X)\mid A=a,Z,X\}
 &=E\!\left[E\{h_a^\dagger(W,X)\mid U,X,A,Z\}\mid A=a,Z,X\right]\\
 &=E\{m_a(U,X)\mid A=a,Z,X\}\\
 &=g_a(Z,X).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Thus \(T_a h_a^\dagger=g_a\) in \(\mathcal G_a\), by the definition of \(T_a\), and consequently \(h_a^\dagger\in\mathcal H_a(P)\), by the definition of \(\mathcal H_a(P)\).

It remains to prove that nonuniqueness cannot change the marginal bridge value.  Let \(h_a\in\mathcal H_a(P)\) be arbitrary and set \(k_a=h_a-h_a^\dagger\in\mathcal H\).  Since both terms solve the same outcome-bridge equation, linearity of \(T_a\) gives
\[
 T_a k_a=T_a h_a-T_a h_a^\dagger=g_a-g_a=0.
\]
At the base law \(P\), \(\mathrm{ass:treatment\text{-}bridge\text{-}existence}\) permits a choice \(q_a\in\mathcal Q_a(P)\), for which the definition of \(\mathcal Q_a(P)\) gives \(T_a^*q_a=1\) in \(\mathcal H\).  Because \(k_a\in\mathcal H\), \(q_a\in\mathcal G_a\), and \(T_a\) is bounded, all inner products below are finite.  The adjoint identity then gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E\{k_a(W,X)\}
 &=\langle k_a,1\rangle_{\mathcal H}\\
 &=\langle k_a,T_a^*q_a\rangle_{\mathcal H}\\
 &=\langle T_a k_a,q_a\rangle_{\mathcal G_a}\\
 &=0.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Therefore \(E\{h_a(W,X)\}=E\{h_a^\dagger(W,X)\}\) for every outcome-bridge representative \(h_a\).

Finally, compatibility and the tower property give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E\{h_a^\dagger(W,X)\}
 &=E\!\left[E\{h_a^\dagger(W,X)\mid U,X\}\right]\\
 &=E\{m_a(U,X)\}\\
 &=E\!\left[E\{Y(a)\mid U,X\}\right]\\
 &=E\{Y(a)\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Combining the last two conclusions for \(a=0,1\), and using the definition of the observed joint-bridge functional in \(\mathrm{def:joint\text{-}model}\), yields for arbitrary \(h_a\in\mathcal H_a(P)\)
\[
 \theta(P)
 =E\{h_1(W,X)-h_0(W,X)\}
 =E\{Y(1)\}-E\{Y(0)\}
 =E\{Y(1)-Y(0)\}.
\]
Thus the observed-law functional is the causal average treatment effect, while its value is invariant to both outcome-bridge and treatment-bridge nonuniqueness.
